name: Frog Pump
description: The frog pump is a floor glute bridge variation performed with the soles of the feet pressed together and knees flared outward, resembling a frog's legs. The externally rotated hip position places the hip flexors and adductors in a lengthened state, reducing their contribution and allowing the gluteus maximus to work in a shortened range with high activation. It is often used for glute activation and high-rep pump work at the end of a training session.

execution.starting_position: Lie on your back with the soles of the feet pressed together and knees fallen outward (externally rotated), forming a diamond shape with the legs. Feet close to the hips.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. A dumbbell or weight plate can be rested on the hips for added resistance.
steps: Step 1: Lie on your back with soles of feet pressed together, knees flared outward. Feet 20–30 cm from the hips.
Step 2: Drive the hips upward by squeezing the glutes.
Step 3: Extend until the hips are fully extended and the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Step 4: Squeeze the glutes hard at the top for 1–2 seconds.
Step 5: Lower the hips back to the floor under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you drive the hips up. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Not fully extending the hips at the top — push all the way up
Letting the lower back arch excessively — posterior pelvic tilt at the top
Allowing the feet to separate — keep the soles pressed together
safety_considerations: Hip discomfort in the externally rotated position may indicate hip flexibility limitations — do not force the range
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip extension at the top. Hips to floor at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the glutes — not the lower back
Push hips fully up — don't stop short
